findings.description: The dot-agnostic retry at truncation.ts:198 applies to every wildcard exclusion pattern the native matcher rejects, not only to patterns that name a tree. On Node >= 22 this silently widens existing operator denylists into dot-led directories: `**/*.yml` or `**/*.yaml` now excludes `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `**/*.json` now excludes `.claude/settings.json`, `.vscode/settings.json` and `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, `**/*.sh` now excludes `.husky/*` hooks. Before this change the native shell dot-file rule kept those paths in the review set, so operators who tuned patterns under that behaviour lose coverage of the most attack-prone files in a repository (CI workflows, agent permission/hook settings, git hooks) with no configuration change on their side. For a review tool, excluding more is the fail-open direction; the implementer's rationale ("hiding dot-files from an exclusion only leaks files into the review set") treats extra review as the harm rather than the safe default. The exclusion is recorded as `excluded_pattern` in the coverage record, but it is indistinguishable from exclusions the native matcher would also have made, so the regression is invisible unless someone diffs coverage records across versions.
findings.failure_mode: An operator on Node >= 22 with a broad wildcard exclusion such as `**/*.yml` or `**/*.json` stops reviewing `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.husky/*` and similar paths after upgrading. A fork PR that edits a `pull_request_target` workflow to exfiltrate secrets, or edits `.claude/settings.json` to add a hook command, passes Bridgebuilder with the file silently marked excluded_pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the dot-agnostic retry so it cannot reach root-level dot-directories by accident: either (a) apply the retry only when the pattern's first segment is a literal that already matched (the reported case `evals/tests/fixtures/**` qualifies; `**/*.yml` does not), or (b) keep a small never-exclude-by-wildcard list (`.github/**`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.husky/**`, `.circleci/**`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.devcontainer/**`) that only a pattern containing an explicit dot-led literal segment can exclude. In either case give retry-only exclusions a distinct coverage reason (e.g. `excluded_pattern_dot`) and log a one-line notice listing them, so the widened denylist is visible to the operator.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator on Node >= 22 with a broad wildcard exclusion such as `**/*.yml` or `**/*.json` stops reviewing `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.husky/*` and similar paths after upgrading. A fork PR that edits a `pull_request_target` workflow to exfiltrate secrets, or edits `.claude/settings.json` to add a hook command, passes Bridgebuilder with the file silently marked excluded_pattern.

findings.description: Non-wildcard patterns are matched with `filename.includes(pattern)` at truncation.ts:197, i.e. an unanchored substring test, and the new test at loa-detection.test.ts:423 now pins that `x/.loa-version.json.bak` is excluded by the pattern `.loa-version.json` as intended, contract-level behaviour. The PR author controls filenames. Any path that merely contains an excluded substring is dropped from the review set: `src/grimoires/backdoor.ts` for the default `grimoires/`, `lib/.claude/run.sh` for the default `.claude/`, `util.loa-version.json.ts` for `.loa-version.json`, or `vendor/evals/tests/fixtures/x.ts` for an operator's `evals/tests/fixtures/` prefix. The LOA_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS tests in the same file show these substring patterns are applied by default when a LOA repository is detected, so in every LOA repo a PR author has a ready-made way to hide a file from Bridgebuilder by choosing its path. This is pre-existing, but this sprint explicitly asserts the over-match as correct, which makes tightening it a breaking change later.
findings.failure_mode: A PR author places a malicious or sensitive change at a path that embeds a default or operator substring pattern anywhere in it. matchesExcludePattern returns true, the file is marked excluded_pattern, and the review never sees it even though it is outside every directory the operator meant to exclude.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor non-wildcard patterns: treat a pattern ending in `/` as a path prefix (`filename.startsWith(pattern)`) and any other non-wildcard pattern as exact filename or basename equality. If substring matching must be kept for compatibility, require an explicit marker (e.g. a leading `*`), and change the test at loa-detection.test.ts:423 to assert the tightened behaviour instead of pinning the over-match. Apply the same anchoring in the Node < 22 branch so the two code paths agree.

findings.description: The lead's review states the compiled regex has "no adjacent ambiguous quantifiers". That holds for the globstar groups, which consume whole `/`-terminated segments deterministically, but not for several `*` inside one segment: `*.*.*.*` compiles to `[^/]*\.[^/]*\.[^/]*\.[^/]*` and a segment that contains many of the literal separator but makes the overall match fail (e.g. 254 dots followed by `/zzz`) forces roughly C(n, k) attempts, where n is the segment length and k the number of literal separators between stars. The filename is PR-author controlled and the regex runs for every (file, wildcard pattern) pair the native matcher rejects, which is the common case. Because `[^/]*` cannot cross a segment and filesystem name length caps n at 255, the cost stays tolerable for k <= 3 (a few million steps) and only becomes a stall for patterns with five or more literal separators between stars, which operators rarely write. The memo map at truncation.ts:149 is also unbounded, but patterns come from config, CLI and `.reviewignore`, so growth is negligible in a per-PR process.
findings.failure_mode: A PR containing many long filenames crafted against an operator pattern with several stars in one segment (e.g. `**/*-*-*-*-*-*.snap`) makes the exclusion pass take seconds to minutes per file, so the review round times out or is reported degraded.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject or warn on patterns with more than three `*`/`?` wildcards in a single segment when compiling in dotSegmentGlobMatch, and cap the filename length passed to the regex (GitHub paths are far shorter than any legitimate limit). Alternatively translate each in-segment wildcard group with a possessive-style structure (e.g. `[^/.]*` when the literal separator is `.`) so the stars cannot overlap the separators they are split on.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR containing many long filenames crafted against an operator pattern with several stars in one segment (e.g. `**/*-*-*-*-*-*.snap`) makes the exclusion pass take seconds to minutes per file, so the review round times out or is reported degraded.
